paper.title: Information Cascades in the Laboratory
paper.note: Bibliographic details beyond title/authors/year (journal, volume, pages, DOI) are not present anywhere in the extracted PDF text and are marked missing in source/paper_metadata.json.

external_source_policy: No OSF or open-materials URL was supplied for this job, so no web search, web fetch, DOI resolution, or repository/author-page lookup was performed. This package was built solely from input/paper.pdf.

empirical_studies.name: Symmetric-design information cascade experiment

conditions.description: Standard sequential urn-prediction task with only private draws; no public information beyond announced decisions.

Same task, but two additional balls are drawn and their colors announced PUBLICLY after the 4th decision-maker's round (procedure fully confirmed in-text only for 2 of these 3 sessions; see audit/missing_information.json).

empirical_studies.sample: 36 decision-making undergraduate subjects (6 per session, University of Virginia economics courses, no prior experience with this experiment) plus 1 non-deciding 'monitor' per session.
empirical_studies.task_summary: Each period, a fair 6-sided die (simulated) selects urn A (2 light/1 dark balls) or urn B (1 light/2 dark balls), equally likely. Six subjects are approached in random order, each sees one private ball draw with replacement, then announces an A/B urn prediction, observable by later subjects. $2 for a correct prediction, $0 otherwise, plus a $5 show-up fee; 15 paid periods per session after unpaid practice periods.
key_measures: Cascade formation rate among periods where a cascade was possible (paper: 41/56)
Reverse-cascade share of formed cascades (paper: 13 of 41 formed cascades)
Status-quo bias check: does the subject follow the preceding decision or their own signal when the posterior is exactly 1/2? (paper: 57 of 68 followed own signal -- no bias detected)
Representativeness bias check, public-draw condition only (paper: 10 of 10 qualifying cases followed Bayes' rule, not representativeness -- no bias detected)
empirical_studies.key_findings_reported: Cascades, including reverse cascades, formed rationally in most possible periods. A round-by-round logit analysis of decision errors (Table 3) shows small but non-negligible error rates that do not change any period's cascade classification. No support was found for status-quo bias or representativeness bias in this setting.

empirical_studies.name: Asymmetric-design information cascade experiment (counting-heuristic test)

conditions.description: Same sequential task, but urn A contains 6 a-balls/1 b-ball and urn B contains 5 a-balls/2 b-balls, so a b-signal is much more diagnostic than an a-signal and a simple count of signal types can disagree with Bayes' rule.

empirical_studies.sample: 36 decision-making undergraduate subjects (6 per session) plus 1 monitor per session; same subject pool/recruitment as study_1.
empirical_studies.task_summary: Identical mechanics to study_1's baseline condition, with the asymmetric urn contents above and no public-draw insertion.
key_measures: Cascade formation rate (paper: 46/66) and reverse-cascade share (paper: 18 of 46 formed cascades)
Counting-heuristic check: when Bayes' rule and simple signal-counting disagree, does the subject follow Bayes' rule? (paper: 41 of 82 disagreement cases, i.e. 50%)
Counting efficiency (paper: approximately equal to actual efficiency, averaged over subjects; 21 of 36 subjects exceeded their own counting efficiency)
empirical_studies.key_findings_reported: Cascades remained prevalent but reverse cascades were relatively more common than in the symmetric design. About a third of all deviations from Bayes' rule can be explained by a simple counting heuristic rather than correct Bayesian updating.

participant_flow.recruitment: Undergraduate economics students at the University of Virginia, no previous experience with this experiment.
participant_flow.per_session_composition: 6 decision-making subjects + 1 randomly chosen monitor (assists with dice/marbles, does not make predictions).
participant_flow.session_structure: Show-up payment ($5) -> instructions read aloud -> monitor selection -> seating behind partitions -> several unpaid practice periods (until each urn selected at least once) -> 15 paid periods, each consisting of a die roll (urn selection, hidden), 6 sequential private-draw-then-announce rounds, and a public reveal of the true urn -> private cash payment at the end (average ~$20 total, monitor +$15).
participant_flow.isolation_and_conduct: Physical partitions and spacing enforced anonymity; subjects were required to remain silent, with early dismissal (paid only cumulative earnings) as the penalty for communicating.

outcomes_overview: Binary per-period cascade classification (none possible / formed normal cascade / formed reverse cascade / possible but not formed)
Per-round decision correctness against the true urn
Expected-payoff-based efficiency measures: actual, private-information-only, optimal, random-choice, and (asymmetric design only) counting-rule efficiency
Status-quo bias and representativeness bias indicator rates (symmetric design)

Round-by-round logit decision-error rates (Table 3) -- reported in the paper, but marked not_ready in evaluation.py because the raw per-subject dataset needed to refit it is not published in the paper and was not sought (no external source authorized)

package_entry_point.task: task/task.json (interaction contract) + task/adapter.py (runnable simulation; supports `python task/adapter.py --smoke-test`)
package_entry_point.evaluation: evaluation/evaluation.py (consumes task/adapter.py's session logs; supports `python evaluation/evaluation.py --smoke-test`)

readiness_status.reason: The package is fully runnable end-to-end (adapter + evaluation smoke tests pass with no network access) and every required file is present, but two categories of researcher decision remain open before this should be treated as a verified, citation-ready replication: (1) study_2_asymmetric's participant-facing instructions are a derived reconstruction, not a verbatim transcript, and (2) the paper's Table 3 logit error-rate analysis cannot be replicated without the authors' unpublished raw dataset. See audit/missing_information.json for the full list (9 items) and suggested next steps.
